findings.title: Hard model-window budget counts only message.content; assistant tool_calls payload is never budgeted
findings.evidence: context_compiler.py:70 (classify_candidates) and :283 (_enforce_hard_budget.total) and degradation_ladder.py:86/_hard_trim_messages all size a message as count_tokens(message.content). base_llm_adapter.py:632 estimate_tokens_for_messages also joins only m.content. Probe P5 (adversarial_scripts/probe_d2.py): an assistant message with content '' and a 200,000-character tool_calls[].function.arguments, compiled with input_budget_tokens=200, returns total_tokens=4, trimmed=False, all four messages kept (200,078 characters of unbudgeted tool_calls).
findings.impact: The 'hard model-window enforcement' claim of R010 does not cover tool-call arguments, function names or role overhead; only the 256-token default margin protects the window. A long agent loop (or a model that writes large arguments) can exceed the real window while every ledger says the context fits.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Count the serialized tool_calls (id, name, arguments) and tool name/role overhead in classify_candidates, _hard_trim_messages, _enforce_hard_budget and the adapter estimator; trim or drop whole tool-call groups when the payload alone exceeds the budget. Add a ce_02 case with a large arguments payload.

findings.title: TASK scope of the memory control plane drops the tenant before the capability call and skips governance
findings.evidence: default_memory_control_plane.py:846-887 (_remember_task/_forget_task): scope.tenant_id is validated against the identity by assert_memory_scope_authorized, then task_memory.write/delete(namespace, key) is called with no tenant, identity or governance evaluation; TaskMemoryCapability (memory_control.py) has no tenant parameter; _assert_identity_tenant_is_bound_tenant guards USER scope only. Probe P3: on one plane/capability, tenant-a writes ns/k, tenant-b overwrites ns/k, tenant-c forgets ns/k -> the key is deleted and all three calls succeed (capability saw only ('ns','k')).
findings.impact: Tenant isolation of task memory is the capability implementer's problem by contract, but the contract gives it no tenant. Any shared task-memory capability collides across tenants (overwrite, read, delete). Latent today: memory_wiring.build_default_memory_control_plane wires only user_profile_manager, so TASK/SESSION scopes are unsupported in the shipped composition.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Extend TaskMemoryCapability with tenant (or identity) and key the namespace by tenant in the plane; apply the same bound-tenant guard and a governance evaluation to TASK scope; add a two-tenant negative test next to test_xd02_*.

findings.title: Only TOOL_OUTPUT was hardened against instruction promotion; RAG, web, memory and attachment fragments still reach the model as role=system
findings.evidence: formatter.py:47-52 renders every fragment that is neither SESSION_HISTORY nor a linked TOOL_OUTPUT as ChatMessage(role='system', content='[context:<source>:<id>] ...'). Probe P2: a RAG fragment 'IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS' is delivered with role 'system'. The R009 fix (provider_lifecycle.py:293-302 rejects TOOL_OUTPUT without tool_call_id; formatter renders linked output as role 'tool') is correctly guarded by tests and by mutant M4 (killed), but retrieved or fetched third-party text keeps system-level authority.
findings.impact: A poisoned document, web page or memory entry that passes (or bypasses, see R008 non-production path) the retrieval-poisoning filter is an instruction to the model, the same class of defect R009 closed for tool output. Mandatory-system protection in the compiler (mandatory_base_message_indices) additionally treats non-fragment system messages as untouchable.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Render untrusted-source fragments (RAG, web search, attachments, long-term memory, knowledge) as delimited data under a non-instruction role or an explicit untrusted envelope; keep role=system for trusted instruction sources; extend the d2 R009 test to every untrusted ContextFragmentSource.

findings.title: Sensitive-data control is provider-declared only: no classifier, no redaction, unclassified fragments default to INTERNAL and egress
findings.evidence: contracts.py:288 ContextFragment.sensitivity defaults to DataClassification.INTERNAL; egress.py filters only CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED against a ceiling hard-coded to INTERNAL (context_engine.py:331 passes no ceiling, no profile option). grep for sensitivity= in intergrax/ finds no producer that classifies memory, RAG, tool or history content (matches are the context contracts/invariants, tests and an unrelated calendar field). Base messages (history, user turn) are not fragments and are not covered. R014 asks that sensitive data is 'classified and redacted'; no redaction path exists in D2 paths. Tests d2 R014 and mutant M3 (killed) prove the filter works for fragments a provider has labelled.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn "sensitivity=" intergrax --include=*.py ; uv run pytest tests/qualification/pdc_x/d2/test_d2_context_fidelity.py -k sensitive
findings.impact: Confidential content flows to an external model unless a provider author labels it; the 'classified' half of the claim rests on every provider doing the right thing, and 'redacted' is not implemented.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Derive sensitivity from the source record (memory governance classification, RAG document classification, tool result classification) at fragment construction; make the ceiling a typed, provider-locality-aware policy; add redaction (or explicit refusal) for classified spans; decide the default for unclassified fragments (fail-closed in strict profiles).

findings.title: Memory retention sweep and RAG freshness are not reachable from any shipped composition; sweep covers USER-profile entries only
findings.evidence: grep over intergrax/, agents/, applications/ (and scripts/ for the sweep names): register_memory_retention_sweep_task, MemoryRetentionSweep, memory_retention_sweep_task_request, RetrievalService(source_observer=...), RetrievalResult.freshness and register_reindex_queue_hook have no caller outside their own modules and tests. memory_wiring.py:619-622 builds the plane with user_profile_manager only. No recurrence/schedule enqueues the sweep. retention_sweep.py:161 lists candidates through MemoryRetentionCandidateReader (user-profile entries); entity-temporal, procedural, long-horizon, session-turn-index and organization-profile memory have no retention enforcement. ADR-PDC-02 says reindexing is 'admitted as background work'; the only mechanism is a process-global synchronous callback list (embedding_version_policy.py:23,157) that nothing registers.
findings.impact: Component behaviour is proven (mutants M5, M6, M8 killed), but in a composed host expired memory is never swept and stale sources are never detected or reindexed: the HIGH-impact FRZ-SEC-09 retention claim is enforced nowhere by default. Same class as P7-00 finding F-04 (opt-in, no production caller).
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Compose the sweep in the host/worker root (task registration + a recurrence rule) and the freshness observer + reindex admission in the RAG composition root; extend retention to the other memory stores or document them as out of scope with an Operator decision; add a composition test that fails when the sweep task is not registered.

findings.title: Citation and evidence fidelity has no enforcing code or discriminating test: CitationChainLink is an unconsumed 28-line model; the cited golden harness only asserts non-empty data

The cited test case 'context golden harness' resolves to tests/unit/runtime/architecture/test_ideal_harness_l3_w2_depth_gate.py: test_ideal_w2_citation_chain asserts len(chain.links)==1 and test_ideal_w2_scenario_and_context_libraries asserts 'cases' is non-empty; tests/fixtures/context_golden/cases.json holds two literal cases and scripts/maintenance/check_context_golden.py prints OK for them. findings.suggested_repair_scope: Either bind CitationChain to the assembled-context ledger (validate fragment ids against fragments_included, excerpt containment, tenant) or reclassify R016 as RAG-citation-only and test fabricated/foreign citations.

findings.title: A raising reindex hook turns a successful retrieval into an exception; hooks are process-global and tenant-blind (P7-00 F-17 confirmed)
findings.evidence: embedding_version_policy.py:157-158 calls every registered hook without try/except; retrieval_service.py:226 evaluates freshness inside the result construction and only the observer call is guarded (:236-253). Probe P4: a hook raising RuntimeError makes RetrievalService._assess_freshness raise RuntimeError. ReindexQueueRequest carries source_path only (no tenant/workspace); the hook list is a module global.
findings.impact: An operator hook failure breaks retrieval for every request that touches a stale source; a multi-tenant host cannot attribute a reindex request to a tenant.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Isolate each hook (log + count), make request_reindex fail-soft in the retrieval path, add tenant/scope to ReindexQueueRequest, scope hooks per service instance.

findings.verification: CODE_READ_BY_AUDITOR (not exploited: no observer is wired)
findings.title: Freshness identity and fingerprint: mutable metadata key, absolute server path stamped into chunk metadata and citations, size+mtime revision (P7-00 F-18 partly confirmed)
findings.evidence: source_freshness.py:149-155 chunk_source_id keys on metadata source_path/source/source_id (callbacks win over the stamp: ingest_pipeline.py `{**freshness_stamp, **callback}`); ingest_pipeline.py:84 stamps source_path=str(path) (absolute) which citation_from_chunk copies into Citation.metadata (citation.py:34-47); observe_file_source (source_freshness.py:130-141) stats the id it is given and uses '<mtime_ns>-<size>' as revision (content edits that keep size and mtime are invisible); a loader-supplied provenance.source_revision in another format than the observer's revision is a permanent false 'stale'. Cross-tenant verdict collapse (the dossier's claim) is not reachable because retrieval is scoped per tenant before the assessment.
findings.impact: Path disclosure to the model/user; a file-stat observer built on chunk metadata is a stat oracle; weak change detection.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Stamp a relative/opaque source id and a content digest, keep the observer key outside caller-writable metadata, document the revision format contract.

findings.title: Retention sweep task: producer-controlled as_of, payload-selected user, unbounded thread join (P7-00 F-15; tenant-fallback claim not reproduced)
findings.evidence: retention_sweep.py:337 as_of_iso from the payload sets the evaluation instant (far future expires every entry that has valid_until or a policy window; forget is irreversible); :331 identity_resolver(tenant, user) is invoked for the payload user_id; :288-291 thread.join() has no timeout. The dossier's 'falls back to the payload tenant' is imprecise: :325 falls back to the queue-admitted `tenant_id` argument and :326 requires body.tenant_id == tenant_id (test_background_retention_sweep_rejects_a_payload_for_another_tenant passes).
findings.impact: Anyone who can enqueue the task inside a tenant can trigger premature irreversible expiry for any user of that tenant; cancellation/deadline cannot interrupt the blocking join.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Drop payload as_of (use the injected clock) or bound it to now+skew, restrict the payload user to the admitted principal or a service identity, add a join timeout/cancellation.

findings.title: Tenant-bound plane guard depends on isinstance(UserProfileManagerMemoryCapability) and a private manager attribute (P7-00 F-36 confirmed)
findings.evidence: default_memory_control_plane.py:213-216 reads self._manager._tenant_id; :379-386 applies the guard only when the capability is that concrete class and only in USER scope. A duck-typed capability, or TASK/SESSION scope (F-D2-02), is unguarded. Mutant M9 (guard no-op) is killed by test_xd02_a_foreign_tenant_identity_on_a_tenant_bound_plane_recalls_nothing.
findings.impact: The guard protects the shipped wrapper only; a replacement capability must re-implement the check.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Add bound_tenant_id to the capability protocol and make the guard protocol-based (fail closed when absent in strict profiles).

findings.title: Required source whose fragments are all egress-blocked fails closed with an untyped ValueError that names the wrong cause (P7-00 F-19 partly refuted)
findings.evidence: Probe P1: request.required_sources={RAG}, only fragment CONFIDENTIAL -> assemble raises ValueError('required source missing after collect: rag') from runtime/policy/context_assembly_policy.py:40 (post-collect policy gate), not RequiredContextSourceUnavailableError. validate_required_sources_fulfilled still runs before filter_fragments_by_provider_egress (context_engine.py:321-334), so the typed validation is satisfied by fragments that are then withheld; the second gate catches it. No silent withholding occurred.
findings.impact: Fail-closed holds; the error class and reason code lose the egress cause (diagnosis, retry classification).
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Run the egress filter before required-source validation or map the post gate error to RequiredContextSourceUnavailableError with reason_code sensitivity.provider_egress_blocked.

findings.title: A provider-declared tool_call_id is only checked for presence: an orphan tool result reaches model-facing context
findings.evidence: provider_lifecycle.py:293-302 accepts any non-blank tool_call_id; formatter.py:33-45 emits role='tool'; merge_iterative_tool_feedback_messages (formatter.py:96) appends unmatched tool messages at the end. Probe P8: TOOL_OUTPUT fragment with tool_call_id 'call-does-not-exist' -> messages [tool(call-does-not-exist), user], linkage violation 'result without call'. The accepted test test_linked_tool_output_stays_a_tool_message_never_a_system_instruction itself uses an unmatched id (call-9).
findings.impact: Many provider APIs reject a tool message without a preceding assistant tool call: a provider can make a run fail (availability). Not an instruction-promotion path.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Validate the id against the assistant tool_calls of the assembled window (drop or fail closed); fix the test to use a matched id.

findings.title: Last-resort hard budget drops the newest non-mandatory messages first and keeps the oldest
findings.evidence: context_compiler.py:345-357 iterates range(len-1, -1, -1). Probe P6: 6 history messages, budget 130 -> kept ['s','h0','h1','u'], dropped h2..h5 (the most recent history).
findings.impact: When the ladder is exhausted the model loses the freshest context and keeps the stalest; contradicts the oldest-first ladder step.
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Iterate oldest-first among non-mandatory units (still dropping tool-call groups atomically) and add an ordering assertion to the R011 compiler test.

findings.title: Weak negative tests in the compaction round trip: broad except-and-return escapes and a reconstruction check against in-test originals
findings.evidence: test_d2_compaction_roundtrip.py:153-156 `except ValueError: return`; :209-212 `except Exception: return`; test_d2_context_fidelity.py:274-280 accepts either an error or an intact instruction; the reconstruction assertion (:125-127) maps source_refs to the in-test `originals`, not to a durable message store. Any unrelated ValueError/Exception makes these tests pass.
findings.impact: Tests can pass for the wrong reason (reduced evidence for R012 and R007 negative cases). Positive round-trip assertions and the other D2 tests were mutation-checked (M1..M9 killed).
findings.suggested_repair_scope: Assert the specific exception type/message (or the typed refusal) and reconstruct from the durable store.
